new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager**

**Manufacturing Operations | Color Compounding and Synthetic Turf Yarn Extrusion**

Company

TenCate

 

Location

Dayton, Tennessee

 

Department

Manufacturing / Operations

 

Reports To

VP of Manufacturing

 

Position Type

Full-Time

**About Us**

TenCate brings together specialized businesses in synthetic turf manufacturing, sports surfacing, construction, and related services. Our operations combine manufacturing expertise, product innovation, and customer-focused execution to support high-performing athletic environments.

**Position Summary**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership and performance of the Dayton manufacturing facility, which includes color compounding and extrusion of synthetic turf yarn. This role has accountability for safe operations, product quality, production performance, cost control, staffing, maintenance coordination, continuous improvement, third-party yarn sales, and sourcing of raw materials.

The Plant Manager will provide strong day-to-day leadership while building the systems, accountability, and capabilities necessary to support future growth. The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader who is comfortable working directly with production teams while also managing plant performance through data and clearly defined operating metrics.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Safety and Compliance**

* Maintain a strong safety culture with clear expectations and accountability at all levels of the plant.

* Ensure compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety requirements and company standards.

* Drive identification and correction of unsafe conditions and operating practices.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead daily operations across color compounding and turf-yarn extrusion.

* Ensure production schedules are achieved while maintaining safety and quality requirements.

* Optimize machine utilization, throughput, labor, and manufacturing efficiency.

* Identify and eliminate production bottlenecks, excessive downtime, scrap, and waste.

* Ensure effective shift-to-shift communication and production reporting.

* Coordinate production priorities with planning, supply chain, quality, maintenance, and other manufacturing locations.

**Quality**

* Ensure products consistently meet established specifications and customer requirements.

* Drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions for quality issues, scrap, and customer complaints.

* Maintain strong process controls around color consistency, raw materials, extrusion conditions, and finished-yarn performance.

* Partner with Quality and Technical teams on process and product improvements.

**Cost and Productivity**

* Manage plant performance against budget and operating targets.

* Drive improvements in labor efficiency, material yield, waste, energy consumption, downtime, and overall manufacturing cost.

* Monitor plant KPIs and develop corrective actions when performance falls below target.

* Identify and execute continuous-improvement and cost-reduction opportunities.

**Commercial and Raw Material Sourcing**

* Manage third-party yarn sales, including customer coordination, pricing support, order execution, and alignment of external commitments with available plant capacity.

* Develop and maintain productive relationships with third-party yarn customers while ensuring service, quality, and profitability expectations are met.

* Lead sourcing and supplier coordination for key raw materials used in color compounding and turf-yarn extrusion.

* Partner with Supply Chain, Technical, Quality, and Finance to evaluate suppliers, material performance, cost, availability, and supply risk.

* Support negotiations, purchasing strategies, inventory planning, and contingency plans that ensure reliable and cost-effective raw material supply.

**People Leadership**

* Provide leadership and direction to supervisors, technical resources, and hourly manufacturing associates.

* Establish clear responsibilities, expectations, and accountability throughout the organization.

* Develop supervisors and future manufacturing leaders.

* Ensure appropriate staffing and training to meet production requirements.

* Create a culture of teamwork, urgency, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Maintenance and Reliability**

* Partner with maintenance to improve equipment reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.

* Establish appropriate preventive and predictive maintenance priorities.

* Support equipment upgrades, capital projects, and manufacturing process improvements.

* Ensure recurring equipment issues receive appropriate root-cause analysis and corrective action.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Use production data and structured problem-solving to drive measurable improvements.

* Establish standardized work and disciplined operating processes.

* Lead improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, output, yield, labor productivity, uptime, and cost.

* Support future capacity planning, equipment additions, and manufacturing expansion as required.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant manufacturing leadership experience in a plant or production environment.

* Demonstrated experience leading hourly manufacturing teams and front-line supervisors.

* Strong understanding of manufacturing KPIs, including safety, quality, throughput, downtime, yield/scrap, labor efficiency, and cost.

* Demonstrated ability to drive operational improvement and hold teams accountable for results.

* Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.

* Demonstrated commercial judgment and the ability to balance customer requirements, plant capacity, material availability, and profitability.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field.

* Experience with plastic extrusion, polymer processing, synthetic fibers, masterbatch/color compounding, or similar continuous manufacturing processes.

* Lean manufacturing or continuous-improvement experience.

* Experience managing a multi-shift manufacturing operation.

* Familiarity with capital projects, process automation, and equipment reliability programs.

* Experience with third-party or business-to-business sales in a manufacturing environment.

* Experience sourcing polymers, additives, color concentrates, packaging, or other manufacturing raw materials.

**Key Measures of Success**

* Safety performance

* First-quality / right-first-time production

* Schedule attainment

* Pounds produced / throughput

* Scrap and waste percentage

* Labor efficiency

* Machine uptime / unplanned downtime

* Manufacturing cost per pound

* Customer complaints and internal quality issues

* Energy consumption per pound produced

* Employee training, development, and retention

* Third-party yarn sales revenue and profitability

* Third-party customer service and on-time delivery

* Raw material cost, availability, quality, and supplier performance

* Raw material inventory and supply continuity

**Work Environment**

This position requires regular presence in a manufacturing environment and the ability to work across shifts as business needs require. The Plant Manager must be able to communicate effectively with hourly associates, technical teams, support functions, and senior leadership.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

The company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to characteristics protected by applicable law.

This description summarizes the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of responsibilities or qualifications. Duties may change based on business needs.

**Job Title:** **VP, Foundry Operations**
=========================================

Posting Start Date: 11/18/26

Job Location(s): Andover, Austin, Greensboro - Thorndike, Hillsboro - Brookwood, Irvine, Richardson, San Jose

If you are looking for a challenging and exciting career in the world of technology, then look no further. Skyworks is an innovator of high-performance analog semiconductors whose solutions are powering the wireless networking revolution. Through our broad technology expertise and one of the most extensive product portfolios in the industry, we are Connecting Everyone and Everything, All the Time.

At Skyworks, you will find a fast-paced environment with a strong focus on global collaboration, minimal layers of management, and the freedom to make meaningful contributions in a setting that encourages creative thinking. We are excited about the opportunity to work with you and glad you want to be part of a team of talented individuals who together are changing the way the world communicates.

Requisition ID: 79081

Job Description:

**Description**
---------------

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

Oversees the operations/manufacturing functions for a group/division or other sub-part of the overall organization, such as a plant. Includes overseeing manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, materials, procurement, and production control, and may also include quality assurance (and, if the incumbent is a plant manager, may include the plant’s finance and administration functions).

**Required Experience and Skills**
----------------------------------

**Desired Experience and Skills**
---------------------------------

The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is currently USD $206,900 - $454,100 per year. Starting base pay will depend on relevant experience and skills, training and education, business needs, market demands, the ultimate job duties and requirements, and work location. Skyworks has different base pay ranges for different work locations in the U.S. Benefits include access to healthcare benefits (including a premium-free medical plan option), a 401(k) plan and company match, an employee stock purchase plan, paid time off (including vacation, sick/wellness, parental leave), among others. Employees are eligible to participate in an incentive plan, and certain roles are also eligible for additional awards, including recognition and stock. These incentives and awards are based on individual and/or company performance.

Skyworks is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Skyworks strives to create an accessible workplace; if you need an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at accommodations@skyworksinc.com.

new_roles.title: VP, Production - Soft Accessories
new_roles.description:
About Us:

Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the hard work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.

**Production**

From sourcing raw materials to manufacturing, order placement, pricing and quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results -driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.

Specific Responsibilities Would Include:

Centric Brands is looking for a dynamic, creative and resourceful Vice President of Production, Soft Accessories, to join its team. This individual must be a self-starter and collaborative leader who takes initiative, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and is excited to accelerate transformation across Centric Brands. The Vice President of Production, Soft Accessories, oversees all facets of global development, manufacturing and supply chain operations for cold weather accessories, including scarves, gloves, hats, beanies and related knit accessories. This leader will identify and manage the appropriate vendors and factories, negotiate manufacturing orders, and ensure the timely delivery of high-quality, profitable goods.

**ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategy & Innovation**

 

* Partner with corporate resources to achieve global production efficiencies across divisions and groups
* Lead ongoing market and competitive research to identify innovations in leather, knitwear, yarns, fibers, fabrications, construction, trims and finishing techniques. Translate relevant developments into actionable recommendations for Merchandising and Design, and maintain a current archive of yarns, materials, hardware and production techniques.

**Operations and Results**

* Oversee and continuously evaluate the approved vendor matrix for cold weather accessories, with particular focus on factories with strong technical capabilities in knit scarves, gloves (knit & leather), hats, beanies and related accessories. Review costing, capacity, quality and production standards.
* Lead high-level negotiations on yarn, material, trim and finished-goods pricing to ensure profitability. Approve final buys; oversee production from development samples through final delivery; resolve vendor non-compliance, claims and chargebacks; and coordinate customs classification requirements with Imports.
* Partner with Merchandising, Design and Sales throughout product development to ensure accurate execution of cold weather accessories, including stitch, gauge, yarn, handfeel, fit, construction, color and finishing. Deliver agreed-upon margin goals and development-calendar milestones across the assortment.
* Review production standards and brand consistency across categories and vendors. Oversee quality-control initiatives, including testing and corrective action plans for yarn performance, pilling, shrinkage, colorfastness, seam strength, embellishments, trims and overall product durability.
* Lead high-level troubleshooting of quality and technical issues. Guide special product development and modifications to designs, materials, stitches and constructions while protecting the intended aesthetic, performance and financial goals.
* Oversee capacity planning and vendor performance by sourcing office, region, country and factory. Define accurate costing models; partner with Sales and Planning to project production needs; make yarn and raw-material commitments when appropriate; allocate production; and reserve factory capacity for seasonal peaks.
* any issues

**Customers & Relationships**

* Partner with customers, Sales, Merchandising and Operations, as well as vendors and factories to ensure adequate flow of goods relative to orders and anticipated demand criteria
* Oversee interoffice communication and follow-up with internal and external customers and contacts regarding production, including suppliers and vendors
* Delegate special projects as assigned
* Travel regularly to factories and international trade shows

**Leadership & Teams**

* Lead, train and motivate global team of full-time and part-time personnel as well as factory and independent agents; strategize staffing needs across categories and brands, where appropriate
* Contribute positively to team dynamic and manage up where necessary
* Attract, develop and retain talent; create appropriate succession plans
* Monitor and evaluate performance of individuals and team(s)

Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have:

* Superior organizational skills and excellent communication skills; team oriented
* Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines, highly detail oriented and meticulous
* Creativity, technical capability and sensibility for merchandising/design
* Required hands-on production and sourcing experience in cold weather accessories, including scarves, gloves (knit & leather), hats, beanies and related knit accessories.
* Bachelor’s Degree
* 10+ years’ experience in production and sourcing; significant relevant experience in category
* Proficient in Microsoft Office, Adobe products, SAP, CAD and Mac computers

Salary Range: $200,000 - $240,000

At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.

**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**

**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager – Manufacturing**

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead an established, mid-size manufacturing operation in Holt, Michigan. This is an opportunity for a well-rounded manufacturing leader to take ownership of the facility's overall business performance, providing strategic direction and leadership while driving operational excellence, profitability, and continued growth.

Reporting to the VP of Operations, the Plant Manager will have full responsibility for the facility's operational and financial performance, including full P&L accountability. This individual will oversee all aspects of the business, lead and develop the management team, and ensure the facility consistently achieves its financial, operational, quality, safety, and customer objectives.

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a seasoned manufacturing leader who understands how to run a plant as a business. The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of operational expertise, financial acumen, and business leadership, with a proven ability to translate company objectives into measurable results.

This person will be comfortable leading through department managers, establishing accountability, making sound business decisions, and developing a culture of continuous improvement. Equally important is the ability to balance the bigger picture with an understanding of what is happening on the plant floor.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Assume full ownership and accountability for the facility's overall performance, including P&L, profitability, operating costs, and financial results.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, and business strategies aligned with company objectives.
* Monitor financial and operational performance, analyze results, identify areas of opportunity, and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Provide leadership and oversight across all plant functions, including production, quality, maintenance, materials, shipping, and safety.
* Lead, mentor, and develop the management team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Provide direction and oversight to the Production Manager and other functional leaders, ensuring alignment across departments and consistent execution of business objectives.
* Drive improvements in productivity, labor efficiency, throughput, quality, on-time delivery, and overall operating costs.
* Identify and implement cost-reduction initiatives, process improvements, and operational efficiencies that positively impact the bottom line.
* Maintain strong customer relationships, ensuring customer requirements are met and issues are addressed promptly and effectively.
* Oversee workforce planning, staffing, employee development, and organizational effectiveness.
* Ensure a safe working environment and maintain compliance with applicable safety regulations, quality standards, and other requirements.
* Direct capital planning and investment decisions, evaluating equipment, technology, and facility improvements to support business needs and long-term growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators, using data and financial reporting to measure results and drive continuous improvement.
* Partner with senior leadership to communicate facility performance, address business challenges, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success managing an entire plant or manufacturing operation.
* Previous full P&L responsibility, including budgeting, financial reporting, cost management, and profitability.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations, including production, quality, maintenance, materials management, and supporting functions.
* Proven ability to improve financial and operational performance through effective planning, execution, and accountability.
* Experience leading and developing department managers and supervisors, with the ability to build a strong, effective leadership team.
* Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand financial statements, evaluate operating costs, and make sound business decisions.
* Demonstrated success with continuous improvement, process optimization, and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Strong customer-facing skills and the ability to develop and maintain productive business relationships.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
* A hands-on, approachable leadership style combined with the ability to think strategically and lead at the business level.

**The Opportunity**

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced manufacturing leader to take ownership of an established operation and make a meaningful impact on its overall performance and continued success. The right individual will have the opportunity to influence the business, develop a strong team, and drive improvements across all areas of the facility.

The company offers a competitive compensation package, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits program including health, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off.

This is an on-site leadership position in Holt, Michigan.

Thank you for considering this opportunity.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

Experience:

* Plant management: 4 years (Preferred)
* P&L responsibility: 4 years (Preferred)
* composite, paint finish, or similar: 2 years (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: VP of Operations – Appliance
new_roles.description:
**Vice President of Operations – Appliance Segment**
----------------------------------------------------

**Company:** SSW Advanced Technologies, LLC 
**Location:** REMOTE, with regular travel to plants in the U.S., Canada and Mexico 
**Travel:** Approximately 30–50% 
**Employment type:** Full-time, exempt

### **About the Role**

SSW Advanced Technologies is a leading manufacturer of engineered components for major appliance OEMs. We’re looking for a **Vice President of Operations** to lead our Appliance Segment, a multi-plant operation that makes wire, glass and component products for some of the best-known names in home appliances.

You’ll be accountable for the safety, quality, delivery and financial performance of our appliance plants across the U.S., Canada and Mexico. That includes:

* San Luis Potosí, MX; Sweetwater, TN; Vincennes, IN; Midland, ON; Clinton, IA & Madison, TN

This is a hands-on executive role for a leader who can set the strategy, build strong plant teams and deliver results for demanding OEM customers.

### **What You’ll Do**

* **Own segment performance:** Drive end-to-end results across all appliance plants against targets for safety, quality, delivery, cost and EBITDA.
* **Set the operations strategy:** Develop and execute a multi-year plan that supports growth, margin expansion and footprint optimization across U.S., Canada and Mexico operations.
* **Lead the customer relationship on operations:** Serve as the senior operations contact for appliance OEM customers, and meet or exceed scorecard goals for quality (PPM), on-time delivery, responsiveness and cost.
* **Deliver launches and changeovers:** Partner with Engineering, Quality and Sales so that capacity, tooling, customer qualification and ramp-up are ready on schedule.
* **Match capacity to demand:** Align production plans with OEM schedules, including seasonal and promotional volume swings, build-ahead requirements and short-notice changes.
* **Partner on supply chain:** Work closely with Supply Chain leadership on commodity exposure, supplier performance, alternate sourcing, inventory, premium freight and cross-border logistics.
* **Drive productivity and cost reduction:** Deliver annual plans that offset customer price-downs and inflation through Lean, automation, scrap reduction and labor efficiency.
* **Manage the numbers:** Build and manage the segment operating budget, capital plan and staffing plan. Hold plant leaders accountable to budget, and lead weekly forecast and commitment reviews.
* **Champion safety and compliance:** Build a zero-harm safety culture and fully implement our integrated Quality, Safety and Environmental management system, 5S and EHS standards.
* **Develop leaders:** Lead, coach and develop Plant and General Managers and operations leaders, and build bench strength and succession for critical roles.
* **Standardize how we run:** Establish common best practices, KPIs and daily, weekly and monthly operating rhythms across all plants.
* **Lead change:** Guide restructuring, footprint and transfer-of-work initiatives, including workforce planning.

new_roles.description:
**About Oshkosh AeroTech, an Oshkosh company**

**Oshkosh AeroTech is a leading provider of aviation ground support products, gate equipment and airport services to commercial airlines, airports, air-freight carriers, ground handling and military customers. Oshkosh AeroTech offers products that make a difference in people’s lives by supporting those in our communities who do some of the toughest work. They own many of the most trusted brands in the air transportation industry, including LEKTRO®, JetAire®, JetPower®, AmpTekÔ, Jetway®, and more.**

The Oshkosh AeroTech Vice President, Operations will lead operational strategy, execution, and continuous improvement across the Ground Support Equipment (GSE) and Jetway businesses. With dual reporting to the VP of Global Operations & Supply Chain at the Vocational segment and the President of Oshkosh AeroTech, this role is a key member of the Oshkosh AeroTech leadership team, responsible for driving a safety culture, operational efficiency, increasing capacity, manufacturing excellence, and overall business performance.

**YOUR IMPACT**

Safety & Operations Leadership

* Develop, implement, and sustain a world-class safety program that prioritizes team member well-being
* Drive a proactive safety culture by embedding safety into all operational activities, ensuring every team member understands and takes ownership of safety responsibilities.
* In collaboration with VP, Operations & Supply Chain at Vocational segment, develop and implement a comprehensive operations strategy aligned with business objectives.
* Establish KPIs to measure and drive operational performance, efficiency, and cost optimization.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives in production, workflow optimization, and resource allocation.
* Ensure world-class manufacturing capabilities, leveraging Lean, Six Sigma, and automation best practices.
* Develop and implement strategy to increase capacity across AeroTech manufacturing sites.
* Partner with Supply Chain organization to optimize supplier partnerships and inventory management.
* Drive cost reduction initiatives while maintaining high quality and regulatory compliance.

Quality & Compliance

* Ensure all operational processes comply with industry standards, safety regulations, and quality control frameworks.
* Implement best-in-class operational processes to reduce defects, improve reliability, and enhance customer satisfaction.
* Drive adherence to ISO and other relevant regulatory requirements.

Financial Management

* Manage budgets, operational expenditures, and capital investments to drive profitability.
* Conduct financial analyses to improve operational decision-making and efficiency.
* Optimize cost structures through strategic sourcing, automation, and process improvements.

Leadership & Talent Development

* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing operations team.
* Foster a culture of safety, continuous improvement, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration.
* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning and development initiatives to align with business growth and expansion.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Engineering, or related field.
* 12+ years of experience in operational leadership, with at least 3 years in a VP or Director-level role.
* Experienced people leader with cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong experience in multi-site manufacturing, supply chain management, and logistics.
* Proven track record in driving operational excellence, lean manufacturing, and six sigma methodologies.
* Strong financial acumen, data-driven decision-making, and process optimization skills.
* Lives the Oshkosh Core Values of We put people first, We do the right thing, We persevere, We are better together
* Demonstrates the Oshkosh Leadership Traits of Inspires Vision and Purpose, Drives Results, Customer Focus, Cultivates Innovation, Fosters Engagement, and Instills Trust

**STANDOUT QUALIFICATIONS**

* Master’s degree in business administration, Engineering, or a related field.
* Experience working with government, military, or defense contracts.
* International or global business experience.

$189,800.00 - $370,200.00

Within this range, individual pay is determined by various factors, including the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate's experience, education and skills, as well as the equity of pay among team members in similar positions. Beyond offering a competitive total rewards package, we prioritize a people-first culture and offer various opportunities to support team member growth and success.

However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with Oshkosh Corporation's legal duty to furnish information.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Compensation:** $130,000–$160,000 base salary, depending on experience and qualifications, plus performance-based bonus..

* Paid time off

new_roles.title: Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology
new_roles.description:
**Experiencing together a unique human adventure**

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Encouraging internal mobility between positions and countries, offering individual development plans and building a partnership based on trust between managers and employees are as many perspectives of motivation for our teams. We also offer them a work environment conducive to exploring new territories and balancing their professional and personal lives. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

**Qualified candidates should possess the following:**

* 8 to 12+ years of Progressively responsible experience in engineering, and production management with a cGMP/FDA-regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Accountable for the definition and execution of the site and regional project roadmap in alignment with business needs and capability.
* Contributes to the selection of the right technology or CMO, taking into account product needs.
* Establish robust cost estimates (CAPEX, resources, future running costs) and planning estimates to support reliable NPVs and commercial strategy.
* Leadership of scale-up batches, engineering batches, and transfer to production.
* Develops manufacturing documentation (Master Batch Records, Submission batch protocols, etc.).
* Reviews and approves transfer and submission files.

**Expected results:** Ensure the robustness and capability of the process transferred to Manufacturing

**Area of responsibility 2: CAPEX Engineering Projects**

**Main activities:**

* Support and lead CAPEX engineering projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Evaluate, scope, and implement CAPEX projects for facility infrastructure, process improvements, and product needs.
* Responsible for managing annual capital budgets and operating expenses for the department.
* Partner closely with key local and global stakeholders (Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, Finance, etc.) to align project execution with regional operational goals.
* Ensure all engineering projects are performed in full compliance with applicable cGMP standards, EHS regulations, and company sustainability objectives.
* Oversee project budgets, engineering designs, contractor selection, and commissioning/qualification timelines.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

**Area of responsibility 3:** Process Improvement & Life Cycle Management (LCM)

**Main Activities:**

* Incorporate structured process improvement concepts (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) across existing product portfolios.
* Lead Life Cycle Management changes to maintain and optimize the existing commercial product portfolio across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Collaborate closely with global and local stakeholders, including Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, and Finance, to evaluate and execute LCM initiatives.

**Expected Results:** Drive continuous product and process enhancement, lower operational costs, ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and extend product life cycles.

**Area of responsibility 4: Validation**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the generation, technical review, execution, and technical approval of validation deliverables (Validation Master Plan, URS, equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, computer system validation)across NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Lead validation projects and teams
* Ensures risk analysis methods are applied to validation activities
* Follow industry and regulatory trends and expectations (GMP, EHS, and sustainability guidelines).
* Review SOPs and batch documentation to ensure adequacy with validation criteria.
* Ensure prompt deviation resolution, including root cause analysis when required.

**Expected results:** A thorough understanding of the validation status of the regional sites, products, and equipment, with proactive remediation plans addressing any gaps.

**Area of responsibility 5: Technical support.**

**Main activities:**

* Troubleshooting and improvement proposal of current commercial products processes (robustness, productivity, cost efficiency & compliance)
* Lean and methodological approach during trouble shooting of complex product/process deviations
* Take ownership of complex product deviation / CAPA until approval
* Contribute to solution design in collaboration with R&D, Quality Assurance, Regulatory, etc.
* Develop, apply and train teams on efficient troubleshooting and optimization methodologies (FMEA,root cause analysis, etc)

**Expected results:** Deliver strong technical and operational process mastery to support manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.

**Area of responsibility 6: Alternate Raw materials**

**Main activities:**

* Technical feasibility assessments and reporting.
* Leads the engineering or validation batches (protocols/reports)
* Coordinates with the other departments (e.g. Quality Control, Regulatory Affairs)to support raw material changes.

**Expected results:** Support strategic sourcing and continuity of supply through alternate raw material qualifications.

**Area of responsibility 7: Packaging**

**Main activities:**

* Leadership of the packaging change controls and CAPAs (eg: alternate packaging components)
* Collaborates with packaging suppliers on new packaging equipment/materials, and technical feasibility assessments…
* Creates packaging specifications, including drawings and written text areas. Prepares and provides cost estimates for new packaging materials.
* Initiates, leads and Implements packaging improvements for existing products to reduce costs and/or improve packaging and product quality.

**Expected results:** Lead packaging design and modifications to drive productivity, efficiency and cost reductions while maintaining all customer and regulatory requirements.

**Area of responsibility 6: Team Leadership**

**Main Activities:**

* Translate team missions into clear, actionable SMART objectives
* Support and coach team members to help them achieve their full potential.
* Evaluate team performance through key indicators and foster a Lean culture.
* Plan and contribute to the continuous development and training of multi-disciplinary team members.
* Implement standard management practices aligned

with Virbac values while promoting a safe, sustainable working environment.

**Expected results:** Define and implement the NORAM Engineering & MSAT vision and organizational structure in alignment with group strategy.

Virbac provides numerous career opportunities, thanks to the diversity of its jobs and their international dimension.

Joining Virbac means joining dynamic teams ambitious for success.

new_roles.title: Sr. Director, Operations
new_roles.description:
**About Schumacher**

Schumacher & Co. is an innovative interior design company that is disrupting the $150 billion-dollar global interior design industry. We are a technological leader on the design frontier, constantly pushing boundaries and striving for excellence. With over 500+ employees and growing, we are driven by a shared belief that design transforms life. We are dedicated to the mission of helping our customers *"celebrate the feeling of home".* F. Schumacher & Co designs and produces some of the most beautiful fabrics, wallcoverings, trims, rugs, furniture, and accessories in the world. Our portfolio of products is broad, but they are united by a passion for design, a thirst for what is next, an appreciation for what's come before, a drive to make our products with enormous care and attention for detail. F. Schumacher & Co is a globally recognized company with a myriad of showrooms both domestically and internationally.

Our competitive advantage in the industry is our people. We believe that our employees are our most important assets. F. Schumacher & Co is deeply anchored in our company's core values which are as follows:

* Preserve our Start-up spirit

* Take Ownership & Accountability

* Be Solutions-Oriented

* Demonstrate Courage

* Practice Adaptability

* Embrace Collaboration

We empower our employees to live these values daily because we understand how it will positively impact the customer's journey. F. Schumacher & Co., also known as FSCO, is the parent company to many brands within our portfolio. This role leads our **Paramount Handprints manufacturing operations** — our internal product mills based in Passaic, NJ and the Brooklyn Navy Yard — which are a critical differentiator for the business, providing craft and flexibility across our portfolio.

**Role Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on **Sr. Director of Operations** to lead manufacturing operations across our two internal product mills: **one in Passaic, NJ** which produces hand screen-printed fabric and wallcoverings in Passaic, NJ, and another in the Brooklyn Navy Yard which prints digital wallcoverings, both for FS&CO and third-party customers. This individual will oversee the full manufacturing process — from receiving and inventory through order entry, craft printing, quality assurance, shipping and client communications.

This is a builder role. The ideal candidate is scrappy and entrepreneurial, comfortable operating in a hands-on, evolving environment, while also bringing rigor, standards, and consistency to a growing operation. They will balance our commitment to craftsmanship with the need for cost efficiency and anticipate that capabilities and capacity will continue to evolve over time.

This role is based full-time, on-site in Passaic, NJ, five days a week, with occasional travel to our Brooklyn Navy Yard and SoHo locations as needed. It reports to the **Head of Portfolio Development**.

 

**What You'll Do**

* **Leadership**: Lead a team of approximately 60 across both mills.

* Directly manage the Director of Production Planning, Director of Production, Shipping & Warehouse Leads, and Senior Digital Printers at each site and indirectly oversee their teams.

* Oversee the CX leader responsible for order entry and client communication.

* Build a strong, accountable culture across both sites; recruit, develop, and retain talent at all levels.

* **Manufacturing Operations**: Oversee the end-to-end manufacturing process and P&L ownership across both sites, including:

* Warehouse receiving and inventory management

* Screen engraving, color mixing, and trialing

* Production

* Quality assurance and printing

* Cutting, packing, and shipping

* **Process improvement & margin management**: Bring consistency and standardization reliability to our operations.

* Balance craftsmanship with efficiency to protect and improve margin across the mills' output

* Identify and implement process improvements that increase throughput, quality, and reliability without compromising craft.

* Develop and manage spending against budget, in conjunction with Head of Portfolio Development

* Identify cost savings opportunities across from raw materials, vendor contracts and labor

* Develop and track KPIs across capacity, production, quality, fulfillment & financial efficiency

* **Facilities, Safety & Space Planning**

* Own facilities, maintenance, and safety programs across both mills.

* Lead space planning as capacity and capabilities evolve over time.

* Identify opportunities to augment capabilities with equipment & CAPEX investment opportunities

* **Collaboration & Communication**: Serve as an internal partner and external-facing representative of the mills, building trust with cross-functional teams as well as third-party customers and vendors.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with key customers and vendors, including third-party manufacturing and supply partners; quickly step into and manage existing external relationships as you transition into the role.

* Partner proactively with Portfolio Development, Design, Procurement, Sales and other cross-functional teams to align capacity and capabilities with business needs.

* Provide proactive, transparent communication and reporting to the Head of Portfolio Development and cross-functional stakeholders

 

**What We're Looking For**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations leadership, ideally in a craft, custom, or make-to-order production environment.

* Ability to consistently balance productivity, quality, and craftsmanship at the highest level.

* Proven experience managing large teams (50+) across multiple functions and/or sites.

* Strong track record in process improvement and bringing standards/consistency to an evolving operation.

* Strong proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

* Excellent people management skills with a demonstrated ability to build culture and develop talent.

* Scrappy, entrepreneurial, and hands-on, balanced with the ability to bring structure and rigor; comfort operating in a business where capabilities and capacity frequently evolve

* Experience with facilities, safety, and space planning oversight.

* On-site, full-time presence in Passaic, NJ required, five days a week, with occasional travel to Brooklyn and SoHo.

* Experience with ERP or production planning software.

* Experience owning a P&L or facility-level cost-center budget.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience in screenprinting, digital printing, or textile/wallcovering manufacturing or adjacent industries.

* OSHA or manufacturing safety certification/experience.

* Bilingual (Spanish)

* Change management experience professionalizing a founder-led or informal operation.

**Benefits Package**

Your well-being is our top priority. Our benefits and total compensation are designed for the whole person, caring for both you and your family.

**Wealth Benefits:**

* Competitive Salary

* Corporate Annual Profit Sharing

* 401K Plan

**Health Benefits:**

* Dental Coverage

new_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**Head of Manufacturing**

**On-Site | Covina, CA | 40 hr/week**

**About Peregrine**

Peregrine Industries builds affordable, U.S.-made autonomous systems for tactical strike, counter-UAS, training, and defense modernization missions. Our platforms include Kestrel and DRACO, backed by PTEC, our modular tactical effects core.

We move fast, hold ourselves to honest engineering standards, and build hardware that has to work the first time in the field.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a hands-on **Head of Manufacturing** to take Peregrine’s production operation from 0 to 1 at our Covina, CA facility. You will stand up the systems, layout, and processes from the ground up, and own how we build quality hardware on schedule as we scale.

This is a hands-on, foundational role. You will work directly with engineering and the production team to turn prototype builds into a repeatable, quality-driven line, set the standards that hold as volume grows, and shape the manufacturing operation that delivers Peregrine’s platforms to the field. The shop floor is the face of the company, and right now it’s close to a blank canvas. How you set it up from the start is how it stays: clean, organized, and tour-ready by default.

**What you’ll do**

* Own manufacturing operations planning across in-house production, contract manufacturing, supply chain, quality coordination, and delivery readiness.
* Build and maintain capacity planning models that surface labor, material, process, vendor, and production bottlenecks before they bite us.
* Set the weekly operating cadence for production, supply chain, and shipment readiness.
* Write the SOPs, production workflows, handoff processes, and accountability structures the facility runs on.
* Establish clear KPIs for output, build cycle time, shortages, rework, supplier issues, inventory accuracy, and on-time delivery.
* Drive improvement projects that lift throughput, cut rework, and improve quality, building the repeatable processes that let us scale without last-minute heroics.
* Partner with engineering to improve assembly, integration, test, and finalization processes.
* Establish the layout, workflow zones, and standards for the Covina facility as it comes online, including designated areas for testing, harness, and soldering work, and clear homes for equipment.
* Maintain flight-ready inventory on site, with a long-term plan and projections to grow as we add hardware and people.
* Coordinate with engineering, quality, and finance so production plans are realistic and executable.
* Build the dashboards and trackers that give leadership a clear read on what’s on track, what’s blocked, and what decisions are needed.
* Help Peregrine move from low-volume builds toward repeatable, higher-volume manufacturing.

**What we’re looking for**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
* 6+ years in manufacturing operations, production management, industrial operations, hardware operations, supply chain, or a related area.
* Experience running or coordinating production in a hardware, aerospace, defense, robotics, electronics, or similar complex build environment.
* Solid grasp of capacity planning, production scheduling, inventory constraints, manufacturing workflows, and operational KPIs.
* A track record of creating SOPs, dashboards, operating cadences, and process improvements in a fast-moving shop.
* Experience working across engineering, production, supply chain, quality, and finance.
* Strong communicator who can drive accountability without leaning only on title or authority.
* Comfortable working in both strategic and hands-on modes on the same day.

**Strongly preferred**

* Experience with UAVs, aerospace, defense, robotics, electronics, or complex electro-mechanical systems.
* Experience manufacturing All Up Round weapons, munitions, energetics, or other regulated hardware under strict quality and safety controls.
* Experience with contract manufacturers, outsourced production, or supplier production readiness.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production planning tools, inventory systems, or manufacturing dashboards.
* Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methods.
* Time spent in a high-growth startup or a scaling hardware company.
* Familiarity with quality systems, receiving inspection, production QC, or supplier quality.

**To apply**

Send a resume to careers@pdxweapons.com

*Peregrine Industries is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status. Position is subject to U.S. export-control regulations; applicants must qualify as U.S. Persons under ITAR.*

Work Location: In person

new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Plant Director**

 

**Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World**

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.

**This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career.**

**The Impact You’ll Make in this Role** 
As a **Plant Director**, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

 

* Leading a team of employees dedicated to making what is indispensable to empower modern life, advance human progress, and deliver a brighter future through 3M Science.
* Overseeing plant environment, health, safety, regulatory and security practices that respect our environment, meet requirements established by regulatory bodies, protect our employees, and align with company expectations.
* Leading operational excellence through conscientious management and decisive actions in environment, health, safety, quality, manufacturing, supply chain, cost, and employee relations.
* Utilizing operational financial acumen to analyze and understand the financial implications of various choices and actions, making informed decisions based on financial data to maximize profits and minimize losses.
* Understanding and applying technology platform fundamentals and principles, thinking strategically, and identifying opportunities to leverage technology for business growth and operational efficiency.
* Accelerating value creation for our customers through responsive end-to-end supply chain performance and prompt resolution to customer inquiries.
* Developing strategic plans and budgets to drive continuous and sustainable improvements through the application of disruptive technology, lean six sigma methods, and effective employee engagement programs.
* Managing inventory, and influencing supplier performance.
* Championing inclusive programs that create a great place to work for all our employees and demonstrating behavior aligned with a work environment in which employees, consultants, and contract workers know that ethical and legal behavior is always expected of them.

**Your Skills and Expertise**

To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:

 

* Bachelor’s degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start) from an accredited institution.
* Ten (10) years of experience in a manufacturing or production facility in private, public, government, or military environment.
* Five (5) years of experience in a plant leadership role.

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

 

* Proven experience in plant leadership roles, demonstrating the ability to drive operational excellence and achieve results.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, quality control, and safety standards.
* Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate teams.
* Demonstrated ability to anticipate future trends, effectively prepare for change, create and communicate change action plans, and implement sustainable change.
* Strategic mindset and the ability to develop and execute plans to meet operational goals.
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities, with a focus on continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
* Bachelor’s degree in physical sciences, Operations Management, or a related field (advanced degree preferred).
* Experience in proven continuous improvement process improvement methodologies.

**Work location:**

* **Onsite, Tonawanda, New York**

**Travel: May include up to 10%** **domestic/international**

**Relocation Assistance: May be authorized**

**Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).**

**Supporting Your Well-being**

3M offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, 3M regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.

**Chat with Max**

For assistance with searching through our current job openings or for more information about all things 3M, visit Max, our virtual recruiting assistant on 3M.com/careers.

This range represents a good faith estimate for this position. In addition, this position may be eligible for a range of benefits (e.g., Medical, Dental & Vision, Health Savings Accounts, Health Care & Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, Disability Benefits, Life Insurance, Voluntary Benefits, Paid Absences and Retirement Benefits, etc.). new_roles.title: Senior Director, CMC-Lead and Product Stewardship, Global Technical Operations
new_roles.description:
**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264447 **Date posted** 16/11/2026

 

**Introduction**

As Senior Director, CMC Product Lead and Head of Product Stewardship, you will lead end-to-end CMC product strategy and the Product Stewardship and Product Champion organization within Global Technical Operations (GTO).

You will lead sophisticated Global CMC programs across development, PPQ, commercialization, and lifecycle management while shaping Product Stewardship capabilities, governance, processes, and talent.

You will guide strategy, manage risk, and drive cross-functional decisions that support product progression and commercial supply.

**What you'll do**

You will lead global CMC operations groups for sophisticated biologics and other advanced modalities across development, PPQ, market rollout, and end-to-end product stewardship. You will define and deliver Global CMC strategies across manufacturing science and technology, manufacturing, analytical, quality, regulatory, technical transfer, and supply activities.

You will lead all aspects of the responsibilities related to Product Stewardship and the role of Product Champion, improving technical and CMC leadership throughout the product lifecycle. Working with BPD, Cross-SET, eGPT, GPT, and Operations teams, you will shape product strategy, influence decisions, and resolve cross-functional issues. Ensure products and processes are scalable, robust, transferable, and ready for commercialization and lifecycle management.

You will advance Early Engagement and drive CoGS strategy, identifying risks early and incorporating yield, process efficiency, manufacturability, network fit, and supply resilience into product decisions. You will also strengthen post-launch CMC leadership across product quality, supply, lifecycle improvements, and post-approval submissions.

You will establish effective governance, decision rights, escalation pathways, role clarity, and ways of working. You will lead all aspects of sophisticated product, technical, quality, supply, and CMC issues and represent Operations, Biologics, and GTO in senior governance discussions.

You will champion data-driven decision-making and the practical use of digital tools, sophisticated analytics, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities. You will build organizational strength through talent development, succession planning, and an inclusive, high-performing culture.

**Essential requirements**

* Degree in a relevant scientific or engineering field.
* 15+ years of leadership experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with deep expertise in biologics, CMC, technical operations, commercialization, product stewardship, or related fields.
* Experience leading sophisticated Global CMC programs, Operations Global CMC teams, major biologics products, or comparable cross-functional technical programs.
* Strong understanding of late-stage development, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation and PPQ, commercialization, control strategy, comparability, lifecycle management, and post-approval change.
* Proven track record to align cross-functional teams within a global matrix.
* Experience leading senior technical teams and building organizational capability through talent development and succession planning.
* Strong enterprise and matrix leadership, with the credibility to influence decisions in senior governance forums.
* Excellent communication and judgment, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly and connect technical decisions with product and business outcomes.

**Desirable requirements**

* Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or engineering field.
* Experience leading Product Stewardship, Product Champion, technical product leadership, or similar product-facing organizations.
* Experience across development and commercial manufacturing networks, including internal and external supply.
* Experience with Global CMC governance, regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and lifecycle management for biologics or complex modalities.
* Experience advancing digital transformation, analytics, automation, or AI-enabled capabilities within CMC, MSAT, Product Stewardship, or manufacturing operations.
* Experience crafting or improving cross-functional processes, frameworks for authority and accountability, and operating models in a global organization.

**Why AstraZeneca?**

At AstraZeneca, we 're dedicated to being a Great Place to Work. Where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and spark your entrepreneurial spirit. There’s no better place to make a difference to medicine, patients and society. An inclusive culture that champions diversity and collaboration, and always committed to lifelong learning, growth and development. We’re on an exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare.

*The annual base pay for this position ranges from $216,996.00-$325,494.00*

*Our positions offer eligibility for various incentives—an opportunity to receive short-term incentive bonuses, equity-based awards for salaried roles and commissions for sales roles. Benefits offered include qualified retirement programs, paid time off (i.e., vacation, holiday, and leaves), as well as health, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.*

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day operations at Innova's M3 facility in Mexicali, Mexico, including production, maintenance, purchasing, shipping and receiving, and site safety. Working closely with the site leadership team, this role ensures production goals, quality standards, cost targets, and customer delivery commitments are met. The Director builds and develops a strong local team, drives continuous improvement, and serves as the key link between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Finance, Quality, and Sales teams. The ideal candidate is based in the San Diego area, is fully bilingual in English and Spanish, and has proven experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico.

 

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Champion and uphold the company's values, mission, and quality policy in all activities.

* Adhere to and help enforce company policies, procedures, and internal control standards.

* Ensure compliance with all applicable Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Follow all safety rules and PPE requirements, and promptly report hazards, incidents, and near-misses.

* Lead all operations at the M3 facility, including production, maintenance, purchasing, and shipping and receiving, to meet production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery commitments.

* Direct and develop the site leadership team, including hiring, training, performance management, and succession planning.

* Oversee production planning and scheduling to balance capacity, labor, and materials with customer demand.

* Establish operational KPIs and monitor productivity, efficiency, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery, taking corrective action as needed.

* Oversee the site safety program and ensure compliance with applicable Mexican health, safety, and environmental regulations (e.g., STPS and NOM standards), fostering a strong culture of safety.

* Develop and manage the site operating budget, labor plan, and capital expenditure requests.

* Oversee equipment maintenance and facility upkeep to maximize uptime and maintain a safe, organized plant.

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve throughput, and lower costs.

* Coordinate with logistics and customs partners to support cross-border shipments, materials flow, and import/export requirements.

* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations, and compliance with Mexican labor law.

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Quality, Finance, and Sales, providing regular operational and financial reporting.

* Perform other related duties as required.

 

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, required.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico (maquiladora or similar cross-border environment) strongly preferred.

* Experience with plastics manufacturing processes (e.g., injection molding, thermoforming, CNC machining) preferred.

* Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification preferred.

 

**SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) required.

* Proven leadership skills, with the ability to build, motivate, and develop a high-performing team.

* Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, and plant management.

* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.

* Financial acumen, with the ability to develop budgets, manage costs, and interpret financial data.

* Working knowledge of Mexican labor, safety, and environmental regulations.

* Working knowledge of quality system requirements under ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ERP/MRP systems.

* Valid passport and ability to cross the U.S.–Mexico border regularly.

 

**TRAINING & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS**

* Complete new-hire orientation and role-specific on-the-job training prior to performing unsupervised work.

* Complete Quality Management System (QMS) training applicable to this role, including quality policy awareness and the consequences of nonconformance to product or process requirements.

* Complete safety training applicable to this role (e.g., PPE use, lockout/tagout, forklift certification).

* Maintain competency through periodic refresher or retraining as required by department procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

 

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Office setting.

* Manufacturing floor environment.

* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses.

 

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

* Mobility to navigate the production floor to conduct inspections and oversight.

 

**EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK**

* This is a full-time exempt position, required to work Monday through Friday. Occasional weekend availability may be required based on business needs.

 

**TRAVEL**

* Regular cross-border travel between San Diego, CA and the M3 facility in Mexicali, with on-site presence required a minimum of 4 days per week.

* Occasional travel to other Innova facilities, customers, and suppliers, up to 10%.
