**Build Your Career with Ashley Furniture- Where Innovation Meets Comfort**
**Who We Are**
At Ashley, inspiring the love of home is at the heart of everything we do. As the world’s largest manufacturer of home furnishings, we’re more than a business — we’re a family driven by innovation, competitiveness, and an unwavering commitment to excellence. We persevere through challenges, push beyond the status quo, and constantly seek better ways to deliver an exceptional customer experience. Our solutions-first mindset and dedication to growth are why Ashley remains #1 in our industry.
  
  
If you’re ready to grow, you’ve come to the right place. With a true “Growth Mindset,” Ashley Furniture invests in developing future leaders and helps every team member learn from the best in the business.
  
  
**If you are a current Ashley employee**
: Please login to your UKG account and apply using the internal job board.
  
  
**Summary**
The Ashley Home Delivery (AHD) Operational Excellence Director provides centralized leadership for operational planning, routing, process development, project execution, vendor governance, performance management, and organizational coordination across Ashley Home Delivery. This role translates strategy into repeatable operating standards, disciplined execution, measurable performance, and scalable support.
  
  
The Director partners with field leadership and cross-functional teams to improve customer experience, delivery performance, carrier accountability, cost effectiveness, and launch readiness, enabling Regional Directors and market leaders to remain focused on field execution.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Planning & Routing**

* Lead the centralized routing organization, establishing operating rhythms, service standards, workload allocation, escalation paths, and accountability.
* Own delivery forecasting, capacity planning, route-planning governance, and resource alignment across AHD markets.
* Develop, document, deploy, and audit routing standards that support safe, efficient, reliable, and customer-focused delivery execution.
* Partner with field leaders to identify capacity constraints, route-quality issues, and execution risks, coordinating corrective actions as needed.

**Operational Excellence**

* Lead the development, maintenance, communication, and adoption of standard operating procedures across Ashley Home Delivery.
* Design and continuously improve end-to-end processes for stand-up, load-out, route monitoring, check-in, returns, recovery, beginning-of-day controls, and end-of-day controls.
* Develop validation, compliance, and audit tools to ensure operating standards are understood, adopted, and sustained.
* Drive continuous improvement through data analysis, root-cause analysis, structured problem-solving, and field feedback.
* Establish governance and documentation processes that preserve institutional knowledge and keep operating standards current.

**3PL & Vendor Management**

* Lead carrier sourcing, due diligence, onboarding, implementation, and performance governance in partnership with Procurement, Legal, Finance, Risk, and AHD leadership.
* Establish consistent business reviews, escalation processes, relationship-management routines, and service expectations for delivery partners.
* Provide leadership for the AHD Claims team and governance of claims administration, disputes, documentation, approval controls, and timely resolution.
* Oversee invoice validation and payment-administration processes, including controls that support accuracy, transparency, and accountability.
* Support contract improvements and ensure approved terms, service levels, and operating requirements are effectively implemented.

**Performance Management**

* Develop and maintain national AHD KPI definitions, reporting standards, scorecards, forecasts, and performance dashboards.
* Establish management routines connecting daily operating controls, weekly business reviews, action plans, and executive-level visibility.
* Analyze performance trends and operational gaps, identify root causes, establish accountable owners, and track corrective actions through resolution.
* Provide decision-ready reporting on customer experience, delivery reliability, productivity, capacity, cost, claims, and carrier performance.

**Strategic Projects & Launch Execution**

* Lead program and project management for AHD market launches, conversions, expansions, and national operational initiatives.
* Establish launch-readiness plans covering schedules, staffing, training, travel, uniforms, fleet, equipment, routing, carrier readiness, communications, and operating controls.
* Coordinate cross-functional implementation activities, manage dependencies and risks, and maintain clear milestones, decisions, ownership, and status reporting.
* Drive post-launch adoption and ensure new processes, tools, contracts, and standards become embedded in routine operations.

**People & Organizational Leadership**

* Lead, develop, and deploy assigned AHD support resources against the highest-priority operational and strategic needs.
* Establish clear roles, decision rights, service expectations, workload priorities, and performance standards for centralized support functions.
* Build a high-accountability, service-oriented culture that partners effectively with Regional Directors, site leaders, carriers, and cross-functional teams.
* Coach and develop team members through ongoing feedback, development planning, and recommendations regarding staffing, selection, recognition, and performance actions in accordance with company policy.

**Qualifications**
**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations, Supply Chain, Logistics, Industrial Engineering, or a related field preferred.
* Equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience may be considered.

**Experience**

* 10+ years of progressive experience in operations, transportation, logistics, supply chain, home delivery, final mile, or a related field.
* 5+ years of leadership experience with responsibility for teams, operational programs, or multi-site/multi-market operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading operational excellence, process improvement, performance management, and large-scale implementation initiatives.
* Experience managing third-party carriers, 3PL providers, vendors, or outsourced delivery operations.
* Experience developing and managing KPIs, scorecards, operating reviews, and performance improvement plans.
* Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional projects from planning through implementation and sustained adoption.

**Additional Qualifications, Preferred**

* Experience in final-mile delivery, retail distribution, home delivery, furniture delivery, or similar customer-facing logistics operations.
* Strong knowledge of routing, capacity planning, delivery forecasting, carrier management, and operational controls.
* Experience developing SOPs, governance frameworks, compliance processes, and audit programs.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate operational data into clear business actions.
* Proven ability to influence field and cross-functional leaders in a matrixed environment.
* Strong project and change-management capabilities with experience managing multiple priorities simultaneously.
* Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.
* Ability to travel as business needs require.

**Benefits We Offer**

* Health, Dental, Vision, Employee Assistance Program
* Paid Time Off; increases with years of service
* Generous Employee Discount on home furnishings
* Professional Development Opportunities
* Tuition Assistance
* Ashley Wellness Centers (location specific)
* 401(k) and Profit Sharing
* Life Insurance

**Our Core Values**

* Honesty & Integrity: Acts with transparency, discretion, and ethical judgment. Trusted to handle sensitive information and provide accurate, unbiased insights.
* Dirty Fingernail: Takes full accountability for outcomes, not just tasks. Inspects details, ensures data accuracy, and follows through to completion.
* Continuous Improvement: Actively seeks better ways to improve templates, tools, and processes. Learns from prior initiatives and embeds lessons into standard work.
* Growth & Results Focus: Understands how transformation initiatives drive growth, cost reduction, and profitability. Keeps work aligned to enterprise priorities.
* Culture of Leadership: Leads through influence, reliability, and example. Builds trust across functions and supports leaders at every level.
* Customer-Centric & Boundaryless: Works across silos for the greater good of the organization. Ensures outputs meet the needs of executives, initiative owners, and teams.
* Operational Excellence: Demonstrates strong organizational discipline, attention to detail, and the ability to translate ambiguity into clear, executable tools.

Overview:

**East Tennessee Behavioral Health** is seeking a dynamic and experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**East Tennessee Behavioral Healt**h is a 90-bed inpatient treatment center serving Knoxville, Tennessee, and the surrounding communities. We provide the highest-quality care for people who have mental health concerns such as depression, anxiety disorders, and bipolar disorder and those who have co-occurring addictions. The acute inpatient treatment we offer supports adolescents, adults, and senior adults, while our outpatient programming serves adults age 18 and older.

**East TN Behavioral Health Hospital** offers an extensive array of benefits to our valued team members. Current offerings encompass:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance coverage
* Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options
* Company-paid Basic Life & AD&D insurance
* Disability benefits
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with a company match
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and Employee Discount Program
* Paid Holidays for work-life balance
* Paid Time Off (PTO)
* Tuition Reimbursement opportunities for career advancement

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
  + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
  + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
  + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
  + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
  + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
  + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
  + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
  + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
  + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
  + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
    - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
    - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
    - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
  + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
  + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
  + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
  + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
  + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
  + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
  + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
  + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
  + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
  + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
  + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
  + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
  + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
  + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
  + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
  + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
    - Changes in policies/procedures,
    - Staffing and assignment changes,
    - Additional education or training for staff,
    - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

existing_roles.title: Director of Quality and Compliance
existing_roles.description:
Description:

The **Director of Quality & Compliance** is responsible for leading LOPA’s overall quality strategy, overseeing the agency’s Quality Management System (QMS) and ensuring that all products, services, and internal processes meet or exceed internal and external customer expectations and regulatory standards. Reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, the position partners with operational leaders to translate requirements and quality findings into effective, measurable practices, fostering an agency-wide culture of integrity and operational excellence.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Quality Strategy & QMS Governance**

* **Quality Management System.** Own, maintain, and continuously improve the agency-wide QMS aligning objectives with organizational priorities and applicable standards.
* **Program Implementation**. Lead implementation and standardization of quality initiatives, establish milestones and accountabilities, monitor adoption, and assess ongoing effectiveness and sustainability.
* **Policies.** Oversee agency-wide development, implementation, including version control, approval workflows for all controlled documents. Support operational owners on content development and enforcement of policies and procedures.

**Regulatory Compliance & Audits**

* **Compliance Oversight.** Monitor compliance with applicable CMS requirements, OPTN policies and FDA regulations and other relevant industry standards and local and federal government regulations.
* **Audit Readiness and Management.** Oversee internal quality audits of donation and business processes to ensure regulatory and policy compliance, leveraging operational data to advise internal stakeholders on corrective actions; ensure ongoing monitoring of implemented changes to assess long-term effectiveness and sustainability. Serve as the primary liaison during external regulatory inspections and customer audits. Oversee agency’s response to any findings or observations from external audit.
* **Quality records.** Ensure quality records and compliance documentation are accurate, controlled, retrievable and inspection ready.

**Continuous Improvement & CAPA**

* **Root-Cause Analysis.** Oversees LOPA’s Occurrence Management Program to investigate instances of procedural non-conformance, resolve systemic issues, and prevent recurrence.
* **Data and KPIs.** Establish quality metrics, track key performance indicators (KPIs), and analyze statistical trends to identify efficiency gains within the QMS.
* **Support Process Optimization.** Partner with Operations leadership and the Performance Excellence team to embed quality and drive excellence in all process improvement initiatives.

**Leadership & Supplier Management**

* **Team Development.** Recruit, coach develop and evaluate a team of auditors and quality team members by setting priorities and performance expectations.
* **Supplier Quality.** Oversee vendor qualification, auditing, and performance monitoring to ensure specifications are met.
* **Customer Relations.** Collaborate directly with customers to resolve quality complaints, review technical specifications, and improve satisfaction.
* **Escalation:** Promptly communicates significant quality or regulatory concerns to CSO and recommend protective or corrective measures.

Requirements:

**Degree.** Bachelor’s degree in Quality Management, Life Sciences, Public Health, Business, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.

**Experience.** Minimum of five (5) years of progressive experience in quality management, assurance and/or control, regulatory compliance, auditing or related functions within a highly regulated environment, including at least two (2) years of supervisor, management or demonstrated functional leadership experience.

**Implementation Experience.** Demonstrated experience implementing, managing or enhancing quality management systems, regulatory compliance programs, or organization quality initiatives required.

**Industry Background.** Proven track record of applying knowledge of the principles of quality assurance/quality control. Experience within healthcare or donation and transplantation preferred.

**Skills & Certifications.** Certified Quality Manager (ASQ CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Black Belt, or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) strongly preferred.

**Technical Expertise.** Deep working knowledge of senior leadership of a Quality System. Experience applying CMS, OPTN, and FDA standards and regulations preferred.

**Leadership.** Exceptional cross-functional communication, strong decision making and problem-solving capabilities; analytical thinker with keen ability to resolve conflict and influence executive stakeholders, adept at managing agency-wide change.

existing_roles.title: DIRECTOR OF ARCHITECTURE & DESIGN QUALITY
existing_roles.description:
**CREATE is growing, and we’re looking for an experienced architect to help us raise the bar.** We’re looking for a licensed architect with 15+ years of experience who loves both sides of architecture: creating great design and figuring out how to actually build it. This is not a business development position. You won’t be expected to bring in work, develop firm strategy, or spend your days networking.

**We want your talents focused on architecture.** You’ll design. You’ll draw. You’ll lead projects. You’ll coordinate consultants. You’ll review drawings. You’ll solve difficult details. And you’ll help establish the level of design and documentation quality that every CREATE project should meet.

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

· Design + Draw (Revit specifically)

· You will remain actively involved in the work.

· We want someone who can take an early idea and develop it into mature, thoughtful architecture, not simply manage the people doing it.

· You’ll work directly in projects, developing concepts, plans, elevations, materials, details and architectural solutions alongside our team.

· We’re looking for someone with a strong design eye who understands proportion, materiality, constructability and the details that make a building feel intentional.

· Lead Projects from Start to Finish

· You’ll provide senior architectural leadership throughout the entire life of a project, from early concepts through construction.

**That includes:**

· Concept and schematic design

· Design development

· Construction documentation

· Code and technical review

· Consultant coordination

· Permitting and bidding

· Construction administration

· Resolving complex design and construction conditions

**Our work includes multifamily, commercial, mixed-use, residential and other project types, with a significant emphasis on multifamily and commercial architecture.**

**Own Design + Drawing Quality**

One of the most important parts of this position is helping define and maintain the standard for CREATE’s architectural work.

You’ll lead our QA/QC process and review projects before major submissions and issuances.

We want you looking at both the big picture and the tiny stuff:

Does the building feel resolved? Are the plans actually working? Do the elevations have the right proportions? Are the details constructible? Are consultants coordinated? Does the drawing set communicate clearly? Would we be proud to put CREATE’s name on it?

You’ll have the authority and responsibility to push projects another round when they aren’t there yet.

**Build the CREATE Standard**

**CREATE is still a young firm, which means you won’t be inheriting 30 years of rigid standards. You’ll help us build them.**

**That may include improving:**

* Architectural detailing standards
* Revit and documentation standards
* Typical assemblies
* Drawing organization
* QA/QC processes
* Design review processes
* Consultant coordination
* Code review
* Specifications
* Constructability review
* Internal design critiques

*The goal isn’t to create bureaucracy. The goal is to make really good architecture consistently.*

**Teach + Mentor**

· We have a growing team of architects and designers, and we want someone who enjoys making the people around them better.

· Sometimes that means redlining a drawing.

· Sometimes it means sitting next to someone in Revit and working through a detail.

· Sometimes it means asking, “Why are we doing it that way?”

· We want someone who teaches through the work—not someone who simply reviews it from across the room.

**WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR**

**Our ideal candidate has:**

* 15+ years of professional architecture experience
* Active architectural licensure
* Significant experience with multifamily and commercial projects
* Strong design portfolio demonstrating mature, thoughtful architecture
* Extensive experience developing construction documents
* Strong Revit proficiency
* Excellent understanding of building assemblies and detailing
* Strong knowledge of building codes
* Experience coordinating structural, mechanical, electrical and civil consultants
* Experience taking projects through construction
* Strong QA/QC instincts
* Ability to identify problems before they become construction problems
* Ability to lead while remaining actively involved in production

**Just as importantly, we’re looking for someone who is:**

· Detail-oriented. Curious. Collaborative. Practical. Confident enough to challenge an idea. Humble enough to listen to another one.

· We don't need perfection or ego.

· We need someone who genuinely cares about getting the architecture right.

**WHERE YOU FIT AT CREATE**

This position works closely with CREATE’s leadership while having a very specific focus: the architecture itself.

Firm vision, business development and growth strategy will remain with Aspen and the ownership team. Operations, staffing and project delivery will continue to be led by Justin, Director of Operations.

Your lane will be architectural excellence: design quality, technical quality, project leadership, documentation and mentorship.

You will have significant influence over how CREATE designs buildings and how we document them, without the expectation that you spend your time selling work or running the business.

**WHY CREATE?**

We’re a small, growing architecture and development firm based in Sioux Falls.

That means this position is different from becoming another senior architect inside a large organization.

You’ll have the opportunity to help shape a practice.

You’ll work directly with the people making decisions. You’ll have meaningful influence over our projects and processes. You’ll be able to design, draw and solve problems instead of moving entirely into management.

**And you’ll help us answer an important question as CREATE grows:**

What should people expect when they see CREATE on a set of drawings or on the side of a building?

We want the answer to be: thoughtful design, technically strong architecture and work we're proud to put our name on.

If that sounds like the kind of responsibility you’ve been looking for, we’d love to talk.

Pay: $99,000.00 - $115,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Relocation assistance
* Vision insurance

Experience:

* Architectural Design : 10 years (Preferred)

License/Certification:

* Architecture License (Required)

Work Location: In person

**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

existing_roles.description:
Overview:

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Quality and Accreditation to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
  + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
  + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
  + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
  + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
  + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
  + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
  + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
  + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
  + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
  + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
    - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
    - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
    - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
  + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
  + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
  + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
  + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
  + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
  + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
  + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
  + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
  + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
  + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
  + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
  + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
  + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
  + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
  + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
  + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
    - Changes in policies/procedures,
    - Staffing and assignment changes,

This role is for an executive leader with experience developing new technologies and bringing high-volume manufacturing facilities to life. You will provide vision, strategy and leadership to help Form achieve manufacturing scale, cost-reduction, and daily operation execution.

The Senior Director of Quality Operations is a strategic and hands‑on leader responsible for ensuring the quality and compliance of all GMP/GDP activities executed internally and by external partners for the company’s products, supporting both clinical trials and commercial distribution, working with the VP of QA, QC and AD

  

This role provides oversight across CDMOs and testing labs, ensuring timely product disposition, investigation management, and quality support throughout the product lifecycle.

The Senior Director QA Operations is accountable and responsible to:

* Represent QA in governance and escalation forums for manufacturing investigations, supplier issues, or product quality events
* Own and continuously improve core quality systems including batch release, deviation/CAPA and change control and ensure scalability.
* Provide Quality Oversight, and support of:
  + Suppliers and other third parties involved in outsourced activities or procured material and services to AKTX, including development and follow up of quality and service agreements.
  + Assigned projects related to product and process development, supply and distribution of medicinal products.
  + Assigned computerized systems and other infrastructure within AKTX group.
* Support, and as agreed lead,

  + internal audits and audits of engaged suppliers and vendors for outsourced activities and of procured services, including planning, and delivery of the audit program.

You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. * Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

**Growth and scale-up**

**People leadership**

Success Measures

You will be measured on aircraft delivery performance, production schedule attainment, factory throughput, labor productivity, manufacturing cost, quality and first-pass yield, safety, production-rate readiness, and workforce development and retention.

Required Qualifications

  

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Aerospace, Operations or a related technical field.

* Proven experience scaling manufacturing from development, prototype or low-rate production to higher-rate production.

OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. Mammoth’s deep science and industry experience, along with a robust and differentiated intellectual property portfolio, have enabled the company to further its mission to transform the lives of patients and deliver on the full promise of CRISPR technologies.

**Position:** Director – Operations  
**Location:** North Carolina/ South Carolina  
**Type:** Full-Time  
**Reports To:** CEO, ZetSol Energy

**Who We Are**

ZetSol Energy is the solar manufacturing and supply chain platform built to give North American solar developers, EPCs, utilities, and independent power producers a reliable, tariff-compliant alternative to fragmented overseas sourcing. The company is establishing a vertically integrated greenfield facility in Tuticorin, Tamil Nadu, producing silicon ingots, monocrystalline wafers, cells, and modules, including high-efficiency TOPCon and HJT technology, and pairs that manufacturing base with a full strategic sourcing, bill-of-materials management, quality audit, compliance, and logistics practice purpose-built for the US market.

ZetSol Energy is backed by Zetwerk, a global manufacturing platform valued at over $2.7 billion that already supplies solar piles, mechanical and structural components, and modules to leading US EPCs and asset owners, and whose 2022 acquisition of Unimacts strengthened its US industrial and solar manufacturing footprint. ZetSol Energy is the next chapter of that build-out: a dedicated US-facing commercial platform launching at a moment when American solar developers are actively searching for supply chain partners who can deliver both scale and certainty.

**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced operations leader to lead and scale ZetSol Energy's US operations, with overall responsibility for manufacturing, factory production, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in managing large-scale operations, with a strong background in Supply Chain Management (SCM), logistics and manufacturing, preferably within the renewable energy, solar or industrial sectors.

This individual will be responsible for overseeing factory production, managing end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, and driving sales operations, including demand planning, order management and customer fulfilment in the US market.

The role will also involve building strong relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, logistics partners and other key industry stakeholders, while ensuring operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and cost optimisation.

This is a key leadership position that will play an instrumental role in building and scaling ZetSol Energy's US operations, establishing robust operational processes and driving business growth in North America.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead and oversee end-to-end US operations for ZetSol Energy, covering manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.

* Manage factory production operations, including production planning, capacity utilisation, quality, productivity and timely delivery.

* Drive end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, including global sourcing, procurement, inventory management, import/export, customs clearance and distribution.

* Oversee sales operations, including demand planning, order management, customer fulfilment and coordination with commercial teams.

* Build and manage relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities, logistics partners and other key stakeholders.

* Ensure compliance with US trade regulations, import policies, tariffs and applicable industry standards while driving operational efficiency and cost optimisation.

* Build and scale the US operations team, processes and infrastructure while working closely with the leadership and manufacturing teams in India.

**Qualifications**

* 15–20 years of experience in operations, manufacturing, supply chain management and logistics, preferably within renewable energy, solar, infrastructure or industrial sectors.

* Extensive experience managing large-scale manufacturing operations, including factory production, production planning, quality and operational efficiency.

* Strong experience in end-to-end supply chain, logistics and sales operations, including global sourcing, procurement, import/export, order management and customer fulfilment.

* Strong understanding of US trade regulations, import compliance, tariffs, customs procedures and logistics frameworks.

* Established relationships with government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities and key industry stakeholders.

* Proven track record of building and managing large operational teams, vendor ecosystems and strategic partnerships, with strong commercial and cost management capabilities.

**Desired Qualifications**

* Experience in the solar, renewable energy or energy manufacturing ecosystem.

* Previous experience leading operations for a global manufacturing or industrial organisation.

* Experience managing manufacturing facilities and cross-border operations between the US and international markets, preferably India.

* Ability to build and scale operational infrastructure in a fast-growing business environment.

**Why ZetSol Energy**

* Opportunity to play a key leadership role in building ZetSol Energy's US operations.

* Work closely with the CEO and leadership team in shaping the company's operational strategy.

* Opportunity to build and scale a large operational and supply chain ecosystem.

* Be part of a growing solar manufacturing and supply chain platform backed by Zetwerk's global manufacturing capabilities.

Benefits:

* Relocation assistance

Work Location: In person

existing_roles.description:
**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.
* Directs and coordinates the preparation of analyses and recommendations regarding policy issues and long-range plans to address ReGen Monterey’s financial needs; advises the General Manager regarding policy issues, programs and projects to meet ReGen Monterey and customer needs; advises and assists the General Manager in identifying, articulating and implementing policies, programs and projects.
* Participates in the analysis of proposed legislation and regulation; participates in industry and intergovernmental activities to influence legislative and regulatory change consistent with ReGen Monterey’s interests and needs; represents ReGen Monterey as requested or assigned in dealings with stakeholders in ReGen Monterey’s service area, and with other industry and governmental agencies and professional organizations.
* Participates in major negotiations with contractors, consultants, vendors, collective bargaining and other public agencies.
* Participates in regional, state, national and other professional meetings and conferences to stay abreast of trends and technology related to ReGen Monterey’s operations, particularly in areas of assigned accountability.

**Knowledge of and Ability to:**

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to successfully perform the assigned duties.

**Knowledge of:**

Principles and practices of recycling and diversion program operations, solid waste management and landfill maintenance practices and procedures; local, state and federal regulations pertaining to environmental management of landfills and public works systems or landfill operations; California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); principles and practices of budgeting, effective management, supervision, evaluation and training; health and safety regulations. Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint) is required.

**Ability to:**

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals; understand highly regulatory issues (current and proposed) and appropriate permitting for solid waste facilities, recycling operations and programs; negotiate with the best interest of ReGen Monterey; work independently with minimal supervision; manage and evaluate the work of others; prepare clear and concise plans, specifications, and technical reports; interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations; present proposals and recommendations clearly, logically and persuasively in public meetings; develop and implement appropriate procedures and controls; exercise sound, independent judgment within policy guidelines; develop and administer departmental goals, objectives, and procedures; analyze and assess programs, policies, and operational needs and make appropriate adjustments; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods and techniques; facilitate group participation and consensus building; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

**TRAINING, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental planning and management; environmental studies; solid waste planning or a related field is required.

**Experience:**

* Ten to 15 years of broad and progressively responsible work experience in recycling program operations, transfer station management, or combined and related experiences.
* A minimum of five years of recent experience in solid waste management and/or in the operation of mixed waste processing facility or a single-stream material recovery facility or operation of a landfill is required. **OR** work experience in a management position with a private or public agency responsible for solid waste management, recycling/diversion or landfill operations to demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities to meet the above minimum requirements.

**License or Certificate:**

* Possession of or ability to obtain a certificate of Manager of Landfill Operations (MOLO) issued by the Solid Waste Association of North America (SWANA) is desired.
* Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required.

**PhYSICAL AND SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:**

The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by employees to successfully perform the essential functions of this class. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Physical Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to sit; talk or hear, in person, in meetings and by telephone; use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; and reach with hands and arms; occasionally bend, stoop, lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 pounds individually. Employees are occasionally required to walk and stand on even and uneven surfaces, grounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Mental Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to use written and oral communication skills; read and interpret complex data, information and documents; analyze and solve complex policy and operational problems; observe and interpret people and situations; use math and mathematical reasoning; learn and apply new information or skills; perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks with constant interruptions; work under intensive deadlines and interact with Board members, all levels of ReGen Monterey management, other elected and appointed governmental officials, consultants, contractors, developers, vendors, employees, media representatives and the public.

**Special Demands**

Must be able to actively participate in public meetings, including giving presentations in person and on camera before the Board of Directors and members of the public.

**Work Environment**

Employees work under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet, occasional exposure to dirt, grease, foul odors and other outdoor elements.
